sentences.text:
Heard Sri.Bhanuprakash.H.V learned counsel for the appellants as well as Sri.B.Pradeep learned counsel for respondent No.2.
2.

Challenge in this appeal is the award that is passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Mysuru in MVC No.884/2022 dated 20.06.2023.
This is a claimants' appeal.

3. Appellant Nos.1 to 3 being majors and married daughters, appellant No.4 being the mother of the deceased Rangamma (hereinafter be referred to as the 'deceased' for brevity) who died in a road traffic accident that occurred in the year 2022, filed a petition claiming compensation of Rs.23,00,000/- in total.
The Tribunal through the impugned award held that appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,30,000/- as compensation.
The version of appellants is that they are entitled to a higher sum.
NC: 2026:KHC:6331 HC-KAR 4.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that he is only aggrieved by failure on part of the Tribunal to add future prospects and awarding meagre sum as compensation towards loss of consortium and funeral expenses.

Learned counsel thereby seeks to pass necessary orders.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 submits that the deceased was aged more than 40 years as on the date of accident.
As per the version of appellants themselves, the elder daughter is aged around 28 years by the date of accident.
Therefore, the deceased will certainly be aged more than 40 years however, the Tribunal took the age of the deceased as 40 years as on the date of accident.
6. The Tribunal placing much reliance on Ex.P7 copy of post mortem report came to a conclusion that the deceased was aged around 40 years as on the date of accident.

As rightly contented by learned counsel for NC: 2026:KHC:6331 HC-KAR respondent No.2, appellant No.2 in the pleadings made a clear mention that her age is about 28 years as on the date of filing of the claim petition.
The accident occurred in the year 2022 and the claim petition also came to be filed in the same year.

Thus, as there is no possibility in the normal course to beget a child by a woman aged around 11/12 years and as the post mortem report reveals that the deceased was aged around 40 years as on the date of accident, this Court is of the view that it can be safely inferred that the deceased should have been between the age group of 41 to 45 years as on the date of accident.

Thus, the appropriate multiplier to be applied as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104 is '14'.
7.

sentences.text: As rightly contented by learned counsel for the appellants, the Tribunal failed to add future prospects.

Having considered the fact that the deceased was aged between 41 to 45 years as on the date of accident, 25% of NC: 2026:KHC:6331 HC-KAR the earnings of the deceased are required to be added towards future prospects as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

Thus, appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,27,500/- towards loss of dependency.

9. Also appellant Nos.1 to 3 are entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- each totalling to Rs.1,32,000/-
towards loss of parental consortium.
Appellant No.4 being the mother of the deceased is entitled to Rs.44,000/- towards loss of filial consortium.
Also, appellants are entitled to Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate.

Thus, the total compensation which the appellants are entitled to receive under each head is as follows:

Loss of filial consortium 44,000-00 Smt. Ambika vs Sri. C.Y. Hemanth on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129406882/
4  NC: 2026:KHC:6331 HC-KAR  4 Funeral expenses 16,500-00  5 Loss of estate 16,500-00
The Tribunal through the impugned order held that the appellants are entitled to a sum of Rs.15,30,000/- as compensation.
However, the discussion went on supra makes it clear that they are entitled to a sum of Rs.18,36,500/-.

Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation that is granted by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mysuru through orders in MVC No.884/2022 dated 20.06.2023 is enhanced from Rs.15,30,000/- to Rs.18,36,500/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till deposit.
NC: 2026:KHC:6331 HC-KAR (iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.
(v) Appellant No.4 is entitled to the entire enhanced sum along with the interest.
(vi) On deposit, appellant No.4 is permitted to withdraw the same.
